items.title: What These 6 Snack and Beverage Stocks Have in Common
items.summary: Coca-Cola and an array of other beverage and snack stocks deliver tasty dividends to income investors.

items.title: How Many Shares of Coca-Cola or PepsiCo Pay $1,000 a Month in Dividends?
items.summary: Key TakeawaysAt today’s prices, collecting $1,000 a month in dividends takes 5,661 shares of Coca-Cola, about $549,100, or 2,028 shares of PepsiCo, about $285,000. PepsiCo looks like the better buy for that income, as long as its turnaround gets its free cash flow growing again.

items.title: 10-Year TIPS Pay 2.77% Above Inflation. Here’s How Dividend Stocks Compare
items.summary: A Treasury coupon can't be cut, but a dividend can grow faster than inflation. Before you pick a side, check the tax bill hiding inside TIPS and the raise that trails inflation at one famous monthly payer.

items.title: The Dividend Investing Strategy That Made Geraldine Weiss a Wall Street Legend
items.summary: Wall Street shut her out, so she signed her newsletter "G. Weiss" and went on to rewrite how investors judge value. Her yield test now splits Coca-Cola, Johnson & Johnson, and PepsiCo, and only one of them tempts her.

items.title: PepsiCo vs. Starbucks: Which Consumer Goods Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
items.summary: Starbucks trades at nearly twice PepsiCo's forward earnings multiple, but its free cash flow and loyalty-driven model raise a sharper question about which premium is justified.

items.title: 5 Dividend Kings to Buy for Lifelong Income Before the End of November
items.summary: A fat yield means nothing if the cash behind it dries up. Five companies with 50-plus years of dividend raises put safety ahead of income, yet one of them leaves almost no room for error.

When policy makers talk about getting “behind the curve” on inflation, investors who react late risk watching others reposition first. items.title: Is PepsiCo (PEP) Facing A Fresh Challenge In Sports Drinks After Its Poppi Deal?
items.summary: PepsiCo (NasdaqGS:PEP) faces fresh competition as Poppi's founders unveil Jetty, a new hydration drink aimed at Gatorade's turf. Jetty is positioned as a lower sugar and lower sodium option for everyday consumers in the mainstream sports drink category. The launch follows PepsiCo's acquisition of Poppi, creating an unusual rivalry between the buyer and the founders of the acquired brand.
